outcome.rationale: Trial is recruiting with primary completion December 2025. No outcome data available pre-cutoff. Primary interest is pain comparison between insufflation systems using novel AI monitoring. Feasibility and safety likely successful; efficacy comparison uncertain without results.

primary_rollup.rule: success=全部主要终点yes；fail=任一主要终点no；其余uncertain

value.estimand: all randomized patients through study completion
value.uncertainty: Single center study, recruitment timeline uncertain, no direct enrollment data available pre-cutoff
value.rationale: Single-center randomized trial with 100 estimated enrollment. Typical robotic prostatectomy trials at dedicated centers complete enrollment within 6-12 months. No direct enrollment status available pre-cutoff.

value.estimand: all treated patients through 30 days post-op
value.uncertainty: Safety monitoring will occur but specific AE rates unknown pre-cutoff
value.rationale: Safety monitoring is standard for all device trials. Both insufflation systems have established safety profiles in laparoscopic surgery. Expected low rates of serious adverse events typical for robotic prostatectomy.

value.uncertainty: Exact values not available; typical ranges for ASA I-III surgical population
value.rationale: Preoperative vitals are baseline descriptive measures. Randomization ensures balance. Expected normal ranges for selected healthy surgical population (ASA I-III, exclusions for uncontrolled hypertension).

value.uncertainty: Exact distribution unknown; typical robotic prostatectomy population BMI 25-30
value.rationale: Baseline descriptive measure. Typical BMI for robotic prostatectomy patients ranges 25-30 kg/m². Randomization ensures between-group balance. No expected difference.

value.uncertainty: Specific values not available; expected normal for selected surgical population
value.rationale: Preoperative labs (FBC, U&E, CRP, PSA) are baseline measures. Exclusion criteria filter for significant comorbidities. Expected normal ranges for selected patients.

value.uncertainty: Pressure stability may differ between devices; Stryker PneumoClear stability at low pressure less established
value.rationale: Protocol specifies 8 mmHg target for both groups. AirSeal valveless system known for pressure stability. Stryker PneumoClear performance at 8 mmHg less documented in literature.

value.uncertainty: No direct comparative data; typical robotic prostatectomy EBL 150-400 mL
value.rationale: Typical robotic prostatectomy EBL ranges 150-400 mL. Low pressure pneumoperitoneum may reduce venous oozing. Between-group difference uncertain; AirSeal may provide more stable conditions.

value.uncertainty: Low event rate; expected <5% but precise comparison unavailable
value.rationale: Blood transfusion uncommon in robotic prostatectomy (<5%). Stable pneumoperitoneum may reduce bleeding. No direct device comparison data available pre-cutoff.

value.uncertainty: Typical range 120-240 minutes; insufflation system unlikely to significantly impact time
value.rationale: Typical robotic prostatectomy procedure time 120-240 minutes. Insufflation system primarily affects pneumoperitoneum stability, not surgical technique. Experienced center expected consistent times.

value.uncertainty: Key differentiating endpoint; valveless AirSeal expected more stable but no direct comparative data
value.rationale: Critical efficacy endpoint. AirSeal valveless design intended for pressure stability. Stryker PneumoClear performance at maintaining 8 mmHg without increase uncertain. Hypothesized AirSeal advantage.

value.uncertainty: Institutional protocol dependent; expected high utilization at specialized center
value.rationale: TAP block standard for postoperative analgesia in robotic prostatectomy at specialized centers. Expected high utilization in both groups per institutional protocol.

value.uncertainty: MME consumption variable by anesthesia protocol; AI-guided monitoring may optimize dosing
value.rationale: Intraoperative analgesia varies by anesthesia protocol. AI-based nociception monitoring (NOL) may guide dosing. Expected 10-30 MME typical for robotic prostatectomy.

value.uncertainty: Novel AI-based measure; no established normative data for robotic prostatectomy
value.rationale: NOL index is novel AI-based nociception monitor. No established normative data for robotic prostatectomy at 8 mmHg. Expected range 10-40 based on general surgical population. Primary between-group comparison of interest.

value.uncertainty: 8 mmHg pneumoperitoneum expected lower PAP than 12 mmHg; between-group difference uncertain
value.rationale: Low pressure pneumoperitoneum (8 mmHg) expected to reduce PAP compared to standard 12 mmHg. Typical PAP 15-25 cmH2O expected. Minimal between-group difference anticipated if pressure maintained.

value.uncertainty: CO2 absorption varies by insufflation efficiency; expected clinically similar values
value.rationale: ETCO2 expected 35-45 mmHg with controlled ventilation. Lower pressure reduces CO2 absorption slightly. Insufflation system efficiency may affect CO2 elimination but expected clinically similar between groups.

value.uncertainty: Enhanced recovery protocols variable; insufflation system effect on recovery time uncertain
value.rationale: Recovery room time depends on institutional protocols and patient factors. Typical range 60-180 minutes. Potential for shorter recovery with better pain control but not established for insufflation device comparison.

value.uncertainty: Primary interest endpoint; low pressure may reduce pain but between-device comparison novel
value.rationale: Postoperative pain is key study endpoint. Low pressure pneumoperitoneum may reduce shoulder/abdominal pain. VAS/NRS expected 2-4 at 24h. Between-group difference is primary study question, uncertain pre-cutoff.

value.uncertainty: Correlates with pain scores; expected 30-60 MME typical for robotic prostatectomy
value.rationale: Postoperative analgesia consumption expected 30-60 MME for robotic prostatectomy. Should correlate with pain scores. Lower pain expected with stable low-pressure pneumoperitoneum.

value.uncertainty: Expected transient postoperative changes; no between-group difference anticipated
value.rationale: Expected transient elevation in WBC and CRP post-surgery. No anticipated difference between insufflation systems as these reflect surgical trauma not device-specific effects.

value.uncertainty: Expected stable vitals; low pressure may reduce hemodynamic variation
value.rationale: Expected stable vital signs post-robotic prostatectomy in selected healthy population. Low pressure pneumoperitoneum may reduce hemodynamic perturbation. No major between-group difference expected.

value.uncertainty: PONV incidence 20-40% typical; multimodal antiemetics standard
value.rationale: PONV incidence 20-40% post-prostatectomy. Multimodal antiemetic protocols standard. No clear mechanism for insufflation system to affect PONV incidence.

value.rationale: Typical robotic prostatectomy stay 1-3 days. Enhanced recovery may achieve 23-hour discharge. Potential for shorter stay with better pain control but not established.

value.uncertainty: Expected low grade I-II 10-20%, major complications <5%; no expected device difference
value.rationale: Expected complication profile typical for robotic prostatectomy: low grade I-II 10-20%, major ≥III <5%. No expected difference between insufflation systems based on mechanism.

value.rationale: Return to OR rare in robotic prostatectomy (<2%). Typically due to bleeding or anastomotic complications. No expected difference related to insufflation system.

value.rationale: 30-day readmission typical 5-10% for robotic prostatectomy. Common causes: urinary retention, infection, anastomotic issues. No expected device-related difference.

value.uncertainty: Documentation will occur; specific AE profile unknown pre-cutoff
value.rationale: CTCAE v5.0 documentation standard for clinical trials. Expected similar AE profile between groups based on comparable mechanism of action and established safety of both insufflation systems.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06915909 is a prospective, randomized, controlled, open-label study comparing AirSeal Insufflation System vs Stryker PneumoClear insufflator for robotic prostatectomy at 8 mmHg pneumoperitoneum pressure. Primary completion date is 2025-12-17 per protocol. Status is RECRUITING. Evidence search returned Europe PMC article MED/42164111 dated 2026-05-18 (post-cutoff, not usable for outcome data). No direct outcome results available pre-cutoff. Using indirect evidence from similar robotic prostatectomy trials and insufflation system comparisons. Evidence role: indirect_direction for most endpoints. Mismatch: articles are post-cutoff or different devices/populations. Numeric use not allowed for precise values. Baseline characteristics (vitals, BMI, labs) expected to be balanced by randomization. Perioperative outcomes (blood loss, procedure time) based on typical robotic prostatectomy ranges. Pain outcomes uncertain due to novel AI monitoring device. Safety outcomes expected low incidence based on standard robotic prostatectomy profile. Major uncertainty: no direct results available pre-cutoff; trial still recruiting; specific effect of Stryker PneumoClear vs AirSeal on pain is investigational. Confidence lowered accordingly.

Endpoint primary-0 (Recruitment rates): Descriptive measure, no directional hypothesis specified. Predict completion of estimated 100 patients over 6-12 months based on typical single-center recruitment rates.

Endpoint primary-1 (Adverse events): Safety monitoring endpoint. Expected low rates of serious adverse events for both devices based on standard robotic prostatectomy safety profile and published insufflation system meta-analyses showing comparable safety.
Endpoint primary-2 (Pre-op vitals): Baseline descriptive measure. Expected normal ranges for ASA I-III patients undergoing robotic prostatectomy. Randomization ensures balance between groups.
Endpoint primary-3 (Pre-op BMI): Baseline descriptive measure. Typical robotic prostatectomy population BMI ranges 25-30 kg/m². Randomization ensures balance.
Endpoint primary-4 (Pre-op labs): Baseline descriptive measure. Expected normal preoperative labs for selected patients (exclusion of significant comorbidities).

Endpoint primary-5 (Insufflation Pressure): Target 8 mmHg per protocol for both groups. Expected mean ~8 mmHg with minimal variation. Primary purpose is maintaining low pressure, not comparing different pressures.
Endpoint primary-6 (Estimated blood loss): Typical robotic prostatectomy EBL 150-400 mL. Low pressure pneumoperitoneum may reduce venous bleeding slightly. Expected similar between groups.
Endpoint primary-7 (Blood transfusion): Low incidence in robotic prostatectomy (<5%). Expected similar between groups, potentially slightly lower with stable pneumoperitoneum.
Endpoint primary-8 (Procedure time): Typical robotic prostatectomy 120-240 minutes. Insufflation system unlikely to significantly impact operative time at experienced center.

Endpoint primary-9 (Need to increase IAP): Key efficacy measure for insufflation stability. Valveless AirSeal may show lower need to increase pressure vs conventional. Uncertain for Stryker PneumoClear comparison.
Endpoint primary-10 (TAP block): Standard anesthetic technique. Expected high utilization (>80%) per institutional protocol, similar between groups.

Endpoint primary-11 (Intra-op analgesia): Measured in MME. Expected 10-30 MME typical. Lower pressure may reduce nociception; AI-guided monitoring may optimize dosing. Uncertain between-group difference.
Endpoint primary-12 (NOL pain score): Novel AI-based measure. No established normative data. Expected intraoperative values 10-40 range. Primary interest is between-group comparison.
Endpoint primary-13 (Peak Airway Pressure): Low pressure pneumoperitoneum (8 mmHg) expected PAP 15-25 cmH2O, lower than standard 12 mmHg. Similar between groups if pressure maintained.
Endpoint primary-14 (ETCO2): Expected 35-45 mmHg with 8 mmHg pneumoperitoneum. CO2 absorption may differ by insufflation system but clinically similar.
Endpoint primary-15 (Recovery room time): Typical 60-180 minutes. Enhanced recovery protocols may shorten. Insufflation system effect uncertain.
Endpoint primary-16 (Post-op pain): Primary interest endpoint. Low pressure may reduce shoulder pain, abdominal discomfort. VAS/NRS expected 2-4 at 24h. Between-group difference uncertain.
Endpoint primary-17 (Post-op analgesia): MME consumption 24-48h post-op. Expected 30-60 MME. May correlate with pain scores.
Endpoint primary-18 (Post-op labs): Expected transient changes (WBC elevation, CRP rise) typical post-surgery. No between-group difference expected.
Endpoint primary-19 (Vital signs 24hr): Expected stable vitals post-robotic prostatectomy. Low pressure may reduce hemodynamic perturbation slightly.
Endpoint primary-20 (PONV): Incidence 20-40% post-prostatectomy. Multimodal antiemetic protocols standard. No clear between-group difference expected.
Endpoint primary-21 (Hospital stay): Typical 1-3 days for robotic prostatectomy. Enhanced recovery may achieve same-day/23-hour discharge. Insufflation system effect uncertain.
Endpoint primary-22 (Complications Clavien-Dindo): Expected low grade I-II complications 10-20%. Major complications (≥III) <5%. No expected difference between devices.
Endpoint primary-23 (Return to OR): Rare event <2% in robotic prostatectomy. Bleeding, anastomotic leak typical causes. No expected difference.
Endpoint primary-24 (Readmission 30-day): Typical 5-10% for robotic prostatectomy. Urinary retention, infection, anastomotic issues common. No expected device-related difference.
Endpoint primary-25 (All AEs CTCAE v5.0): Comprehensive safety capture. Expected similar profile between groups based on mechanism of action similarity.
